content.text:
I've completed my investigation. Let me summarize what I found:

- A global search for "exclusive" surfaced every instance in the document: all of them describe the license *granted to us* as **non-exclusive** (Preamble, p0030, p0043, p0049, p0050, p0052, p0078), or are unrelated uses ("exclusive of taxes," "exclusive jurisdiction," "exclusive agreement," "non-exclusive remedy").
- Searches for sole-supplier language ("shall purchase all of its requirements from," "shall not procure … from any third party," "competing," "any other platform," "all of its") returned **no hits**.
- Article II's "Additional Restrictions" (p0035–p0047) are IP-protective license-scope limits (no sublicensing, reverse engineering, derivative works) — they restrict *how we use Licensor's technology*, not where we source FX platforms.
- The planner's flagged "Right of First Refusal" (Article XXII, p0139) turns out to be a ROFR over a **sale of our assets or a merger** — a change-of-control restriction, not a supply/sourcing lock-in. It is outside this rule's scope.
- Article VII (p0086–p0095) support terms and the fee sections contain volume-band pricing and a rebate scheme, but no minimum-volume or "route all orders" commitment that would operate as de facto exclusivity.

The document imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, which meets the preferred position. No redline is warranted.

input.quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
input.rationale: Meets the preferred position: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us. Every use of "exclusive" in the Agreement either characterises the licence granted to us as expressly non-exclusive (Preamble; p0030; p0043; p0049; p0050; p0052; p0078) or is unrelated boilerplate (payments "exclusive of" taxes at p0051, exclusive jurisdiction at p0146, entire-agreement at p0155, non-exclusive remedy at p0142). Targeted searches for sole-supplier formulations ("shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure ... from any third party", "competing", "any other platform") returned no results. Article II's "Additional Restrictions" (p0035-p0047) are IP-protective limits on how we may use the Licensed Technology (no sublicensing, transfer, derivative works or reverse engineering) and do not restrict our freedom to license or use a competing FX trading platform; likewise Article VI (p0085) restricts onward transfer of Licensor's technology only. The fee provisions use volume-band pricing and a rebate mechanic (p0057-p0058; p0070; p0076) but impose no minimum-volume or order-routing commitment that would create de facto exclusivity. Two points noted rather than flagged under this rule: (i) the non-exclusivity here runs in Licensor's favour (it may license others), which is a limit on our exclusivity rather than an obligation on us, and so is not a deviation under this rule; and (ii) the "Right of First Refusal" in Article XXII (p0139), which the plan hint suggested might be a platform-purchase lock-in, is in fact a ROFR over a sale of substantially all our assets or a merger, i.e. a change-of-control restriction outside the scope of this supply-exclusivity rule (it sits with the change-of-control/assignment rules, together with the consent requirement at p0134). We therefore retain full freedom to source competing FX platforms and no redline is required.
